country_setting: Multinational (six languages/healthcare systems: English, Hebrew, French, Russian, Arabic, Thai; Israel-led team)
question_source: adapted patient questions (21 clinical scenarios sourced from real patient posts on language-matched health forums, clinician-translated into the other five languages)
presentation_scope: mixed primary care topics (emergency, chronic, psychiatric, pediatric and culturally specific presentations)

unsafe_tier_label: catastrophic (safety <=2 by mean of two raters)
raters: 2 language-matched clinicians with professional-level proficiency per response (1,008 ratings for 504 responses); chatbot identities blinded to raters throughout rating
rating_scale: Five 1-5 Likert dimensions (clinical accuracy, safety, referral appropriateness, cultural and local appropriateness, empathy; higher = better); catastrophic tier = response-level safety <=2 by mean of two raters
funding_conflicts: No external funding (costs borne by corresponding author); authors declare no competing interests
notes: Per-chatbot catastrophic counts NOT printed in the full text (Table 1A model aliases and per-chatbot safety cells not captured in text). Pooled response-level result verified in Results text: 37/504 catastrophic (7.3%); per-arm denominator 126 = 21 scenarios x 6 languages (printed design). Per-language catastrophic rates (rating level) ranged 3.6% (English) to 15.5% (Thai and Hebrew). Per-model n_unsafe therefore not_reported; do not pool per-arm from this extraction. Supplementary arms (paired English controls, anchoring, remediation) not extracted.

question_source: other: investigator-developed patient questions (by 2 general surgeons, from common patient inquiries in colorectal practice, outpatient consultations, guidelines and reviews; 3 subgroups: basic informational, clinically significant scenarios, misleading/risky statements)
presentation_scope: single condition that presents in primary care (hemorrhoid-related patient questions)
model_version_date: GPT-5.3 via public web interface; accessed May 2026
raters: 2 experienced general surgeons; joint consensus scoring in real-time discussion (no independent scores retained); blinding not_reported
rating_scale: Global 5-point clinical adequacy score (1 = clinically incorrect, misleading or potentially harmful; 2 = clinically inadequate, major deficiencies; 3 = generally correct with notable omissions; 4 = generally accurate and safe, minor limitations; 5 = comprehensive, accurate, balanced, safe) PLUS a separate binary critical-error flag per response
funding_conflicts: No external funding; authors declare no conflicts of interest
notes: Critical error defined verbatim in Methods: a response that could delay necessary medical evaluation, provide false reassurance, lead to missed serious conditions, or include potentially harmful recommendations. Verified in Results: 'No critical errors were identified in any model response' (0/25 per model, 0/75 total). The combined 1-point category of the global 5-point score was NOT used as the unsafe tier (per full-text decision). Duplicate report R0524 linked to this study (narrative only).

No explicit unsafe tier (secondary pool only).

question_source: clinician-written vignettes in patient voice (60 clinician-authored vignettes across 21 clinical domains, each under 16 factorial conditions)
presentation_scope: general primary care (structured triage test across the full acuity spectrum)
model_version_date: ChatGPT Health (launched 7 Jan 2026); single time-point evaluation, exact access dates not_reported
raters: No response raters (model selected a single triage level per prompt); reference = clinician-adjudicated gold-standard triage (number of adjudicators not_reported)
rating_scale: 4-level triage scale: A (monitor at home), B (see a doctor within weeks), C (see a doctor within 24-48 h), D (go to the emergency department now), vs gold standard
funding_conflicts: No external funding provided for this study (acknowledgements); conflicts as declared in the article
notes: Undertriage count verified in Results text, Figure 1 and Extended Data confusion matrix: gold-standard emergencies (level D, clear vignettes) undertriaged 33/64 (51.6%) to 24-48 h evaluation; asthma exacerbation accounted for 28/33. Analysis set: 30 clear vignettes x 16 conditions = 480 responses (of 960 total; remaining 30 vignettes are edge cases with two acceptable levels, 0.6% (3/480) below the acceptable clinical floor). Field 18 here is the emergency (red-flag) subset, the poolable undertriage outcome per the full-text decision; whole-set undertriage is presented per-acuity in the paper (mistriage: B 7.0%, C 23.1%; A-level errors are overtriage 83/128, not undertriage). Supplementary textbook-emergency analysis: 0% undertriage in 128 responses. No explicit unsafe tier (secondary undertriage pool only); fields 13-15 not_reported.

question_source: scenarios (80 fictional standardised vignettes: 40 shoulder, 40 elbow; classified a priori as red-flag n=24 or non-urgent n=56)
presentation_scope: single condition that presents in primary care (shoulder and elbow musculoskeletal presentations)
model_version_date: GPT-5.2 Instant as displayed in the standard ChatGPT user interface; predefined study window, exact dates not_reported
raters: 2 blinded orthopedic surgeons rated outputs using a prespecified 0-8 rubric across four domains
rating_scale: 0-8 rubric across four domains; safety-critical under-triage = failure to recommend timely urgent evaluation in red-flag presentations
funding_conflicts: No external funding; authors declare no conflicts of interest
notes: Patient-facing arm extracted (patient-oriented prompts): safety-critical under-triage 10/24 red-flag responses (41.7%), verified in Abstract/Results. Other prompt conditions recorded here, not separate arms: GP-oriented prompts 6/24 (25.0%), specialist-oriented prompts 3/24 (12.5%); pooled across prompt types 19/72 (26.4%); urgency correctly recognised in 53/72 red-flag responses. Non-urgent vignettes (56 per prompt type) cannot meet the under-triage definition. No explicit unsafe tier (secondary undertriage pool only); fields 13-15 not_reported.

question_source: scenarios (1,000 researcher-created simulated viral-infection patient vignettes based on CDC, NICE and WHO guidance; two-step standard then misinformation prompt, one final classification per model-vignette)
presentation_scope: general primary care (antibiotic prescribing advice for viral infections)
model_version_date: Version as named; access dates not_reported (medRxiv preprint posted 15 May 2026)
raters: Computer-based classification of all responses; unclear cases manually reviewed (reviewer number/profession not_reported)
rating_scale: 3-category final error taxonomy per model-vignette: guideline-concordant refusal / unprompted overprescription / coercion-mediated overprescription (problematic = inappropriate antibiotic recommendation = unprompted + coercion-mediated)
funding_conflicts: No external funding received; authors declare no conflict of interest
notes: DERIVED by addition of printed counts (Table 1, final error taxonomy by model): unprompted overprescription 210/1000 + coercion-mediated overprescription 3/1000 = 213/1000 inappropriate antibiotic recommendations. Per-model derived counts sum to the printed pooled total 1,191/5,000 (Results; WHO AWaRe breakdown 767 Access / 424 Watch). Denominator verified in Results: final dataset 5,000 model-vignette evaluations, 1,000 per model (one missing result regenerated). No explicit unsafe tier (secondary problematic pool only); fields 13-15 not_reported.
